crime_highlights: Ms. Atwood was by the rear passenger side of Mr. Desmond’s vehicle, opening the rear door, when the vehicle struck her.
She was then dragged under the vehicle. Mr. Desmond continued to reverse into the correct lane of travel
Ms. Atwood was taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries.
She suffered fractures to her cervical spine, resulting in paralysis from her neck down.
rationale_highlights: I conclude there is certainly some connection between Mr. Desmond’s circumstances and his cultural background.
I understand and have considered the systemic and background factors impacting Mr. Desmond.

I agree with the representations made by his counsel: “There is an overrepresentation of Black persons in custody in Canada as a result of systemic discrimination and its lifelong impact on those from racialized backgrounds.”
note: Court only says it considered background; never states effect on sentence.

crime_highlights: Mr. B. would show E.D. explicit pornographic material on his cellphone, both videos and pictures
the sexual incidents escalated in frequency between 2017 and 2022 and became an almost daily occurrence, whenever Mr. B. would have access to E.D. alone
she felt afraid during these incidents
rationale_highlights: The Gladue report sets out that both communities in which Mr. B. was raised have been historically disadvantaged.
Considering the circumstances, the aggravating and mitigating factors, the principles of sentencing and Mr. B.’s background, I find a fit and proper sentence to be 40 months incarceration.
I find this sentence best reflects his moral culpability in these circumstances.
note: Background cited for sentence below Crown's 4 years; Crown conceded mitigation.

crime_highlights: Mr. Willis broke into her home through a basement window in the middle of the night and proceeded to choke Ms. Harding to death with a pair of her jeans.
She was completely defenceless in her own home against the onslaught of violence she encountered in the early morning hours of July 10, 2020.
Ms. Harding’s dead body was left on the hallway floor, only to be discovered by her son, Mark Harding, more than a day later.
rationale_highlights: the moral culpability of an African Nova Scotian offender has to be assessed in the context of historic factors and systemic racism
Mr. Willis has endured racial discrimination as a black man living in Nova Scotia as well as other parts of the country.
Nevertheless, I am mindful of the points raised in the IRCA along with the caselaw describing the “worst of the worst” cases
In all of the circumstances I have decided that this case falls in between the first and third timeframes: i.e., 15 – 20 years.
note: Listed under mitigating; IRCA cited for rejecting Crown's 22 years.
